description:
## Goal

Make blocked-wait expansion and product-pull wait handling independent of wait iteration order, then remove the two Debug-text scheduling barriers.

## Verified current state

At origin/main `a3a9761d1209165e5230625b9347cf6b0ad09b83`, two production paths still order work with raw `Debug` text:

- `compiler2/product_drive.rs:138` sorts `Vec<PullWait>`;
- `compiler2/deps.rs:289-295`, in `WorkGraph::unresolved`, sorts waits by `(format!("{:?}", fact), readiness)`.

The second sort moved from `drive.rs`; `drive.rs` now consumes the ordered result in both `demand_blocked_wait_producers` and the stall loop.

These are not cross-process canonical keys. `PullWait` and `FactKey` variants can contain `ExecutableKey`/`ActivationKey`, whose `arrow` is a raw interned `Ty`. `semantic::StableSortKey` documents why sorting such identities by `Debug` is not cross-process stable.

Current comments distinguish two facts: demanding a set of producers is commutative with respect to which producers are requested; request order currently controls FIFO job order and can affect an order-sensitive downstream merge. That is no longer a textual contradiction. It identifies the defect boundary: the loops need an order-independence proof before either barrier can be deleted.

## Evidence boundary

fz-kdt.34 has landed, so identity and causality are available in the public trace. Use those identities in the regression.

Do not treat raw type-arena numbering differences as proof of a semantic or artifact difference, and do not attribute existing callable-construction cache-hit redistribution to these loops without a causal trace connecting it to one of these wait-order barriers.

The current tree has no focused test presenting the same waits in several explicit orders and comparing settled products/backend output. Until that test is red, this remains a verified unsafe scheduling dependency, not a reproduced output divergence.

## Strategy

1. Add seams/harnesses that feed identical blocked waits and product waits in forward, reverse, and seeded orders.
2. Compare settled fact/product values, canonical product identities, causal work multisets, and byte-identical backend programs.
3. If order changes an answer, trace the first differing fact/product and repair the order-sensitive join or ownership rule.
4. Once every tested order agrees, remove both Debug-text scheduling sorts.
5. Preserve explicit ordering only for presentation/diagnostics; separate that concern from scheduler execution order.

Do not replace either barrier with canonical rendering or another global scheduler sort.

## Acceptance

- Forward, reverse, and multiple seeded blocked-wait orders settle identical fact states and canonical causal-work multisets.
- Equivalent product-wait orders settle identical product values, requested product identities, and backend programs.
- Both Debug-text scheduling sorts are absent from production execution paths.
- Diagnostic presentation remains deterministic without controlling execution.
- Target fixtures pass across separate processes and interp/run/build.
- Full library, single-threaded fixture matrix, determinism gates, and clippy with warnings denied are green.
- Fact-engine/product-drive documentation states that wait processing order is not semantic input.
title: Remove Debug-text wait sorting after proving blocked-wait and product-pull order independence
